lines:
Responsibilities: Connects only to configured, core-attested MCP servers and manages initialize/feature negotiation, session reuse, tools/resources/prompts discovery, approved calls, progress, cancellation, and teardown over MCP. MCP remains a tool/resource/prompt protocol and is never treated as a universal external-agent lifecycle.
Owned runtime state: bounded sessions keyed by exact server binding/version/hash and host generation, negotiated protocol/capability snapshot, request-ID correlation, in-flight limits, reconnect/backoff state, and health observations. Discovered catalogs are runtime evidence, not canonical configuration.
Versioned ports and contracts: McpServerManifestV1, McpSessionSpecV1, McpCapabilitySnapshotV1, McpCallV1, McpRawEventV1, ForwardableMcpSetV1, and CloseSessionV1. Catalog/schema drift from the frozen descriptor blocks affected calls rather than mutating workflow definitions.
Failure and degraded behavior: initialization timeout, protocol violation, vanished tool, incompatible schema, transport loss, or exhausted restart budget produces explicit degraded/definite-not-started or uncertain outcomes according to dispatch milestones. Reconnect never silently repeats an effectful call.
Security truthfulness: secret slots and workspace exposure are lease/envelope-bound; configured local MCP servers may themselves be trusted user-level processes and are not a sandbox unless an explicit isolation backend enforces one.
Observability, performance, and cross-platform behavior: bounded request/notification queues, progress coalescing without semantic reordering, session/latency/error metrics, redacted protocol diagnostics, MCP stdio/HTTP backpressure, and normalized stdio/environment behavior on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
Non-responsibilities: no server installation/enablement, external-agent continuation or approvals, workflow node creation, authority grant, provider fallback, canonical catalog/history persistence, or automatic call retry.

data.name: MCP Client & Session Manager
data.technology: Rust MCP client pool over stdio and HTTP transports
